title: Finite temperature effects on g-modes of inviscid neutron stars
comment: 14 pages, 12 figures
summary: We study the effect of temperature on secular, compositional $g$-modes in the core of inviscid neutron stars. Using a chiral $SU(2)_f$ sigma model, we construct isentropic temperature profiles for hot and dense matter and find that the frequency of the global core $g$-mode's dependence on temperature is governed by the nuclear symmetry energy slope parameter $L$. As a result, the $g$-mode frequency of a warm neutron star can be either higher or lower than that of its cold counterpart, depending on $L$. Our results highlight the interplay of thermal effects and composition gradients, and demonstrate the potential of neutron star $g$-mode observations to constrain the density dependence of the symmetry energy.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how temperature affects neutron star core g-mode frequencies, revealing their dependence on the nuclear symmetry energy slope parameter L, and suggests g-mode observations could constrain nuclear matter properties.
AI.motivation: To understand how temperature influences the secular, compositional gravity modes (g-modes) in neutron star cores and to explore the connection with nuclear symmetry energy.
AI.method: Used a chiral SU(2)_f sigma model to construct isentropic temperature profiles for hot, dense neutron star matter and studied the temperature dependence of g-mode frequencies.
AI.result: Found that the frequency of core g-modes depends on temperature through the nuclear symmetry energy slope parameter L, causing the frequency in warm neutron stars to be higher or lower than in cold ones depending on L.
AI.conclusion: Thermal effects and composition gradients in neutron stars interplay significantly, and g-mode observations can potentially constrain the density dependence of nuclear symmetry energy, providing insights into neutron star interior physics.

title: Sensitivities of Black Hole Images from GRMHD Simulations
comment: 16 pages, 12 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: The advent of high-fidelity imaging of supermassive black holes calls for efficient and robust data-analysis methods. In this work, we use $\texttt{Jipole}$, a differentiable, $\texttt{ipole}$-based radiative transfer code, to enable gradient-based analyses of images generated from state-of-the-art general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations. We compute image sensitivities, i.e., pixel-wise derivatives of the intensity with respect to model parameters, which form the Jacobian of the forward model and define a local map from parameter space to image space. Using these sensitivities in a mock data analysis, we find that GRMHD-based images generate a structured error landscape for parameter fitting, with anisotropies and local minima, making parameter exploration nontrivial but still tractable when guided by gradient information. We characterize this landscape through the Jacobian and assess the feasibility of gradient-based recovery under idealized, blurred, and noisy conditions. Our results show that automatic differentiation-computed image gradients can guide parameter exploration effectively even in the presence of noise. These findings establish a basis for efficient, high-precision model--data comparisons in black hole imaging and motivate the integration of these sensitivities into advanced inference frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a differentiable radiative transfer code to calculate image sensitivities from GRMHD simulations of black holes, showing that gradient-based parameter fitting can effectively navigate complex error landscapes even with noise, paving the way for improved black hole image analysis.
AI.motivation: The need for efficient and robust data-analysis methods in the context of high-fidelity imaging of supermassive black holes.
AI.method: Using Jipole, a differentiable ipole-based radiative transfer code, to compute pixel-wise image sensitivities (the Jacobian) from GRMHD simulations, enabling gradient-based parameter analysis.
AI.result: Gradient-based parameter recovery is feasible and effective even under noisy and blurred conditions, with the Jacobian revealing a structured, anisotropic error landscape containing local minima but still navigable with gradient information.
AI.conclusion: Automatic differentiation-computed image gradients facilitate efficient and high-precision model-data comparison for black hole imaging, motivating their incorporation into advanced inference frameworks.

title: An XMM-Newton Analysis of the Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidate MCG+11--11--032
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We investigate the possibility of a binary supermassive black hole system at the center of MCG+11--11--032, a local (z = 0.036) Seyfert 2 galaxy. Prior work with stacked Swift/XRT spectra suggested the presence of two Fe K$α$ lines (at 6.16 keV and 6.56 keV) with 2$σ$ confidence. This could be consistent with a prediction of several hydrodynamical models, in which each black hole hosts a mini-disk and contributes one Doppler-shifted Fe K$α$ line to the total spectrum. Another study using a single exposure from Chandra/ACIS did not find evidence for a double line. Here, we conduct follow-up with two epochs of XMM-Newton/EPIC data spaced $\sim$6 months apart. After fitting our spectra with models from the previous two studies, we do not find evidence for a double iron line in either observation. Our best-fit model yields $Γ= 1.63^{+0.20}_{-0.21}$ and $N_\text{H}/10^{22} \text{ cm}^{-2} = 17.9^{+2.7}_{-2.4}$ for the first epoch, and $Γ= 1.46^{+0.22}_{-0.24}$ and $N_\text{H}/10^{22} \text{ cm}^{-2} = 17.1^{+2.7}_{-2.4}$ for the second. We compare our spectral parameters with those derived in past work on this source, finding broad agreement with prior datasets. Lastly, we discuss the properties of MCG+11--11--032 alongside samples of Seyfert 2 galaxies from the literature, finding that it is consistent with this population and the single AGN scenario.

AI.tldr: Follow-up XMM-Newton observations of MCG+11--11--032 show no double Fe Kα lines, contradicting prior indications of a binary black hole system; spectral analysis supports a standard single AGN interpretation.
AI.motivation: To investigate the presence of a binary supermassive black hole system in the Seyfert 2 galaxy MCG+11--11--032, specifically to verify prior hints of double Fe Kα lines which may indicate two black holes each hosting a mini-disk.
AI.method: Analysis of two epochs of XMM-Newton/EPIC X-ray spectra spaced ~6 months apart, fitting spectral models previously applied to this source, and comparison with prior Swift/XRT and Chandra/ACIS observations.
AI.result: No evidence was found for the previously reported double iron line feature in either XMM-Newton epoch. Spectral fitting yielded consistent parameters with past studies and indicated that the source's properties align with single AGN Seyfert 2 galaxies.
AI.conclusion: The data do not support the presence of a binary supermassive black hole system in MCG+11--11--032, and its X-ray spectral characteristics are consistent with a single AGN scenario typical of Seyfert 2 galaxies.

title: Spectral index evolution of the limb-brightened jet in 3C 84
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures; accepted for publication by A&A
summary: Relativistic jets launched by active galactic nuclei are fundamental for understanding the physics of accreting supermassive black holes and their immediate environment, yet the mechanisms driving jet launching remain uncertain. In this study, we investigate the sub-parsec jet of 3C 84 using multi-epoch, multi-frequency, very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations with the European VLBI Network and the Very Long Baseline Array at 22 and 43 GHz. We analyse the evolution of the spectral index gradient in the core region to relate the observed structure to physical interpretations and to discriminate between competing jet launching models. Furthermore, we examine the impact of the ambient medium and magnetic field configuration on jet morphology and dynamics over time, and explore their connection to a coinciding $γ$-ray flare. Our spectral analysis reveals significant changes across three epochs, indicating dynamic activity between filamentary structures on sub-parsec scales, evolving magnetic fields, and a complex interaction with the surrounding medium, all of which shape the innermost jet and may influence its high-energy emission.

AI.tldr: This paper uses multi-frequency VLBI observations of 3C 84's sub-parsec jet to study spectral and structural changes, revealing dynamic magnetic and environmental interactions that influence jet launching and high-energy emission.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanisms driving relativistic jet launching from active galactic nuclei, specifically in the sub-parsec jet of 3C 84, through detailed observational analysis.
AI.method: Multi-epoch, multi-frequency very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations at 22 and 43 GHz using the European VLBI Network and the Very Long Baseline Array, analyzing the spectral index gradient evolution in the core region and assessing the impact of ambient medium and magnetic field configuration on jet morphology and dynamics.
AI.result: The spectral analysis showed significant changes over three epochs, revealing dynamic activity between filamentary structures on sub-parsec scales, evolving magnetic fields, and complex interactions with the surrounding medium, which influence the innermost jet structure and its high-energy emission.
AI.conclusion: The study provides insights into the physical conditions shaping the sub-parsec jet of 3C 84, highlighting the interplay of magnetic fields, ambient medium, and filamentary structures that impact jet morphology and possibly the origin of coincident γ-ray flares, helping to discriminate between competing jet launching models.

title: A sample of short-lived Galactic radio transients from ASKAP VAST
comment: Submitted to ApJ
summary: Galactic radio transients (GRTs) are mysterious short-lived (~days to months) radio transients that are quiet at all other wavelengths. Until now, roughly half a dozen such sources have been reported, predominantly towards the Galactic center. However, no unifying properties have been identified among these, leaving their nature, emission mechanism, and even classification poorly understood. Due to the lack of periodic and uniform radio observations over wide areas of the Galactic plane until now, the sample size of such transients remained limited. Here, we use radio observations from the Australian SKA Pathfinder's Variables and Slow Transients survey to discover six new radio transients along the Galactic plane that resemble GRTs. Detailed investigation of archival data suggests that these sources may be divided into two classes: sources that exhibit sporadic, pulse-like (minutes) radio emission, and sources that exhibit long-term (weeks) flaring-type radio emission. For the short-time variable sources, we draw similarities between optically bright long-period radio transients and our sample to propose wide-orbit (~days) white dwarf binaries as underlying sources. For sources that show long-term outbursts, we draw comparisons between dust-obscured outbursts from WD binaries and our sample. These results could imply that the ongoing wide-field radio surveys are uncovering radio emission from sub-populations of WD binaries that were previously unexplored.

AI.tldr: Using ASKAP survey data, six new Galactic radio transients were discovered and categorized into two types linked to white dwarf binaries, indicating these surveys are revealing new populations of radio-emitting binary systems previously unexplored.
AI.motivation: To address the limited sample size and poor understanding of Galactic radio transients (GRTs) due to lack of wide-area, uniform radio observations along the Galactic plane.
AI.method: Utilized radio observations from the Australian SKA Pathfinder's Variables and Slow Transients survey to identify new radio transients and analyzed archival data to characterize their emission properties and possible classifications.
AI.result: Discovered six new Galactic radio transients resembling previously known GRTs and identified two classes based on emission behavior: sporadic pulse-like emissions and long-term flaring-type emissions, linking these to wide-orbit white dwarf binaries and dust-obscured outbursts in such binaries respectively.
AI.conclusion: The study suggests that the newly discovered GRTs represent sub-populations of white dwarf binaries emitting radio waves, implying that ongoing wide-field radio surveys are uncovering previously unexplored sources and emission mechanisms among Galactic radio transients.

title: Model-Independent Analysis of Type Ia Supernova Datasets and Implications for Dark Energy
comment: To be submitted to JCAP. Comments are welcome. Flux-averaging code to be publicly released; currently available by request
summary: Recent analyses combining DESI DR2 BAO with CMB and SNe Ia data have reported $2.8$--$4.2σ$ evidence for dynamical dark energy, but the significance depends strongly on the supernova sample, raising the question of whether this signal reflects new physics, dataset-specific systematics, or the choice of dark energy parameterization. We investigate this question by analyzing four SNe Ia compilations (Pantheon, Pantheon+, DES-Dovekie, and Union3) with DESI DR2 BAO and Planck CMB distance priors, using flux averaging, model-independent expansion rate extraction, parametric ($w_0 w_a$CDM) fits, and a non-parametric reconstruction of the dark energy density ratio $X(z) \equiv ρ_{\rm DE}(z)/ρ_{\rm DE}(0)$. Flux averaging reduces the $Ω_m$ difference between SNe and DESI from ${\sim}2σ$ to ${\sim}1σ$ for Pantheon+ and DES-Dovekie. The reconstructed $X(z)$ for DESI DR2 + CMB + SNe is consistent with $Λ$CDM for Pantheon, Pantheon+, and DES-Dovekie except at $0.5<z<1$, consistent with Wang \& Freese (2026). The largest deviation occurs at $z=2/3$, reaching ${\sim}2.7σ$ for Pantheon+ but only $1.6$--$1.7σ$ for Pantheon and DES-Dovekie. The $X(z)$ for DESI DR2 + CMB + Union3 is consistent with these within $1σ$, but shows an additional $2.4σ$ deviation at $z=1/3$ besides the ${\sim}2.7σ$ deviation at $z=2/3$. Across all analyses, the departure from $Λ$CDM correlates with each dataset's $Ω_m$ preference. We demonstrate that a pure $Λ$CDM universe with the measured $Ω_m$ differences can reproduce the observed $X(z)$ pattern, providing a viable alternative interpretation of the observed $X(z) \neq 1$ pattern. Future surveys by Euclid and Roman with sub-percent $Ω_m$ constraints will be essential to determine whether the signal reflects genuine dark energy evolution or residual inter-probe $Ω_m$ inconsistencies.

AI.tldr: Current evidence for dynamical dark energy from combined cosmological datasets varies by supernova sample and correlates with matter density preferences; this pattern can be explained without invoking dark energy evolution, emphasizing the need for more precise future measurements.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the reported $2.8$--$4.2σ$ evidence for dynamical dark energy from combined DESI DR2 BAO, CMB, and SNe Ia data reflects new physics, dataset-specific systematics, or parameterization choices.
AI.method: Analyzed four SNe Ia compilations (Pantheon, Pantheon+, DES-Dovekie, Union3) combined with DESI DR2 BAO and Planck CMB distance priors using flux averaging, model-independent expansion rate extraction, parametric ($w_0 w_a$CDM) fits, and non-parametric reconstruction of the dark energy density ratio $X(z)$.
AI.result: Findings show $X(z)$ consistent with $Λ$CDM except deviations around $z=2/3$ varying by SNe dataset, with deviation magnitude correlated to each dataset's $Ω_m$ preference. A pure $Λ$CDM universe with measured $Ω_m$ differences can reproduce the observed $X(z)$ deviations.
AI.conclusion: The apparent dynamical dark energy signal may reflect residual $Ω_m$ inconsistencies among datasets rather than genuine dark energy evolution. Precise future surveys (Euclid, Roman) with sub-percent $Ω_m$ accuracy are crucial to resolving this ambiguity.

title: Distinct First-to-Second Peak Yield Ratios and Timescales Reveal a Sub-dominant Prompt Channel
comment: Comments are welcome
summary: Stellar abundances reveal non-monotonic [Y/Eu] and [Sr/Eu] evolution, a systematic decline with increasing [Eu/H] at low metallicity, a minimum at $[\rm{Eu/H}] \sim -0.3$ and then a rise at high metallicity. This behavior requires at least three distinct neutron-capture sources operating on different timescales. We develop a one-zone chemical-evolution model constraining their typical delay-times, rates, and yield ratios. Reproducing the observed $\rm{[Y/Eu]}$ and $\rm{[Sr/Eu]}$ sequences requires, a delayed $r$-process channel (most likely binary neutron-star mergers) dominating Eu production ($\gtrsim 95\%$ of total Eu). A prompt channel preferentially producing first-peak elements with minimal Eu, explaining the increasing [Y/Eu] at decreasing [Eu/H] below $[\rm{Eu/H}] \lesssim -2.5$; and delayed AGB $s$-process enrichment with delays greater than $t_{min} = 0.3-0.6$\,Gyr reproducing the late-time upturn in Y (Sr). Our model quantitatively reproduces all constraints, including the large $Δ[\rm{Y/Eu}] \approx 0.6$ dex variation between the late-time rise [Eu/H] and the minimum value, the location of the minimum at [Eu/H] $\sim -0.3$ and late-time rise. The first-to-second peak yield ratios correspond to $[\rm{Y/Eu}] \approx -0.3$ (prompt) and $\approx -0.8$ (BNS mergers). The observed $Δ[\rm{Y/Eu}]$ amplitude establishes a model-independent lower limit on the first to second peak yield ratio $\gtrsim 3.4$ between the prompt and delayed channels, ruling out models with similar prompt and delayed yield ratios. These results demonstrate that explaining the observed heavy-element abundance patterns requires multiple channels with distinct nucleosynthetic signatures and operational timescales, providing constraints on the relative rates, delay times, and yield patterns of candidate production sites.

AI.tldr: The study models heavy-element abundance variations in stars, revealing at least three neutron-capture sources with distinct yields and timescales, notably binary neutron-star mergers dominating Eu production, a prompt channel for first-peak elements, and delayed AGB s-process contributions, explaining observed abundance patterns and constraining nucleosynthetic processes.
AI.motivation: To understand the non-monotonic evolution of heavy-element abundances in stars, specifically the variations in [Y/Eu] and [Sr/Eu] ratios with metallicity, reflecting distinct nucleosynthetic processes.
AI.method: Developed a one-zone chemical-evolution model that constrains delay-times, rates, and yield ratios of neutron-capture sources by quantitatively reproducing observed abundance sequences.
AI.result: Identified three neutron-capture sources with distinct timescales: a delayed r-process channel (binary neutron-star mergers) producing most Eu; a prompt channel producing first-peak elements with minimal Eu; and delayed AGB s-process enrichment causing late-time element increases. The model matches observed abundance variations and establishes stringent limits on yield ratios, ruling out models with similar prompt and delayed yields.
AI.conclusion: Heavy-element abundance patterns in stars require multiple nucleosynthetic channels operating on different timescales with distinct yield signatures. This provides quantitative constraints on the rates, delay times, and yields of candidate astrophysical production sites, critically informing nucleosynthesis and chemical evolution theories.

title: Effective field theory of a single scalar pion field for large scale structure in the Universe
comment: 35 pages, 9 figures
summary: We discuss the effective field theory of large scale structure in terms of a single scalar degree of freedom, corresponding to the velocity potential of the matter fluid in a $Λ$CDM universe. This cosmic ``pion'' field is nonlinearly related to the overdensity and the gravitational potential, and corresponds to the Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken spacetime symmetry, allowing us to organize perturbation theory in a systematic way while keeping the symmetries manifest. We develop the effective field theory of the pion field to next-to-leading order, and we use it to calculate the corrections to the power spectrum and to check that these are consistent with the consistency relations of spontaneously broken spacetime symmetry. We compare our results against computer simulations for the evolution of large scale structure in the pion field picture, and we make use of N-body simulations to measure EFT coefficients and analyze the growth of additional degrees of freedom in the deep nonlinear regime. We conclude with a discussion of how the pion field picture may help suggest new variables for analyzing simulations and experimental surveys of large scale structure.

AI.tldr: This work develops a symmetry-based effective field theory of large scale structure using a scalar pion field representing the matter velocity potential, producing consistent power spectrum corrections validated against simulations, and proposing new analysis tools for cosmological data.
AI.motivation: To provide a systematic, symmetry-preserving framework for analyzing large scale structure evolution in the universe by describing it through a single scalar field related to matter fluid velocity potential in a ΛCDM universe.
AI.method: Formulate the effective field theory (EFT) of large scale structure using a pion field as the Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken spacetime symmetry; develop the EFT to next-to-leading order; calculate power spectrum corrections; verify consistency with symmetry relations; compare results with N-body simulations to measure EFT coefficients and study nonlinear regime effects.
AI.result: Successfully organized perturbation theory via the pion field EFT, obtained power spectrum corrections consistent with spontaneously broken symmetry constraints, measured EFT coefficients from simulations, and identified the potential of the pion field approach to propose new variables for analyzing large scale structure in simulations and surveys.
AI.conclusion: The pion field EFT framework provides a powerful and systematic tool for understanding large scale structure formation, preserves key symmetries, aligns well with simulations, and can guide future analysis of cosmological data using new variables inspired by the pion field representation.

title: Beyond the Diffusion Coefficient: Propagators and Memory in Cosmic Ray Transport
summary: Cosmic ray (CR) transport is usually modeled with a single diffusion coefficient, but this description captures only the growth of the variance and not the full transport process. Distinct transport mechanisms can share the same effective diffusion coefficient while producing different particle distributions and approaches to the diffusive limit. This limitation is especially relevant in realistic multiphase, structured, and time-dependent media, and is also reflected in observed environmental variations in CR transport near pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants, and molecular clouds. Particle-tracing studies also show clear departures from standard diffusion, including both superdiffusion and subdiffusion. We therefore develop a propagator-based framework centered on $P(x,t)$, the probability distribution of particle positions, or equivalently its Fourier-Laplace transform $P(k,s)$. This object is compact and statistically complete, and naturally exposes memory: the CR flux can depend on earlier gradients when unresolved trapping or phase changes are coarse-grained away. Using the Montroll-Weiss formalism, we show how to measure $P(k,s)$ directly from trajectories, how to recover the associated memory kernel, and how to represent broad kernels efficiently with a Prony expansion. Applied to a multiphase medium, the framework shows that slow regions can regulate escape without dominating the total residence-time budget. We also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport, and show that if trapping structures evolve while particles are still sampling them, the static long-time limit need not be reached. This paper provides the foundation for future observational applications, particle-tracing measurements, and CR-MHD closures.

AI.tldr: This work develops a propagator-based framework for cosmic ray transport going beyond single diffusion coefficients, capturing memory effects and complex transport behaviors like super- and subdiffusion in multiphase media through new theoretical and computational methods.
AI.motivation: Traditional cosmic ray transport models use a single diffusion coefficient, which fails to capture the full transport dynamics and particle distributions, especially in complex, multiphase, and time-dependent environments.
AI.method: The authors develop a propagator-based framework focused on the probability distribution of particle positions P(x,t) and its Fourier-Laplace transform P(k,s). They employ the Montroll-Weiss formalism to extract P(k,s) from particle trajectories, recover memory kernels, and efficiently represent broad kernels with a Prony expansion. They also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport.
AI.result: The framework reveals that slow regions regulate particle escape without dominating residence time, and evolving trapping structures prevent reaching a static long-time diffusion limit. This approach allows for capturing non-standard transport behaviors such as superdiffusion and subdiffusion.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a compact, statistically complete framework for cosmic ray transport that incorporates memory effects and broad transport kernels, improving over classical diffusion models and enabling better modeling of cosmic ray behavior in structured and evolving environments.

title: Beyond the Standard Model of Cosmology: Testing new paradigms with a Multiprobe Exploration of the Dark Universe
comment: 8 pages, no figs, accepted for publication in Symmetry
summary: Cosmology is living through fascinating times, where new observations from ground and space telescopes are questioning the established paradigm, the so-called Lambda Cold Dark Matter model. The particle nature of Dark Matter is severely constrained by underground experiments, while recent observations by galaxy surveys indicate that the cosmological constant (Lambda) may not be constant after all. Furthermore, observations at high redshift of fully-formed galaxies with massive black holes at their centers by the James Webb Space Telescope, as well as black holes with unexpected properties observed by gravitational wave detectors LIGO-Virgo, are driving an in-depth revision of our assumptions in models of structure formation and the evolution of the universe. I propose to explore two new paradigms to account for Dark Matter and Dark Energy, based on known physics without the need for new particles nor new degrees of freedom. I will extend the primordial spectrum of fluctuations to small scales with new statistical properties to provide a viable Primordial Black Hole scenario for Dark Matter, and will include non-equilibrium thermodynamics in the expanding universe, in the form of General Relativistic Entropic Acceleration, to explain Dark Energy. My proposal could provide a unified explanation for a plethora of interrelated multi-epoch, multi-scale and multi-probe observations from present and future Gravitational Wave detectors, Large Scale Structure observatories and Cosmic Microwave Background experiments. It emphasizes the need to develop new theoretical ideas hand-in-hand with observations to acquire a deeper understanding of our universe. If these ideas are correct, they will open a new window into the early universe and a new fundamental understanding of gravity in the late universe.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes new physics-free paradigms for Dark Matter and Dark Energy, using Primordial Black Holes and entropic acceleration to reconcile recent cosmological observations challenging the standard model.
AI.motivation: Recent observations challenge the Lambda Cold Dark Matter model, including constraints on Dark Matter particles, possible variability of the cosmological constant, and unexpected properties of black holes.
AI.method: The author proposes to extend the primordial fluctuation spectrum with new statistical properties for a Primordial Black Hole Dark Matter scenario and incorporate General Relativistic Entropic Acceleration from non-equilibrium thermodynamics to explain Dark Energy.
AI.result: This approach offers a unified explanation for diverse observations across different epochs and scales, linking Gravitational Wave detections, Large Scale Structure, and Cosmic Microwave Background data.
AI.conclusion: If validated, these new paradigms could revolutionize understanding of the early universe and gravity in the late universe by providing a particle-free explanation for Dark Matter and Dark Energy.

title: Hybrid Simulations of Supersonic Shear Flows: II) Cosmic Ray Viscosity
summary: In this second paper in a series dedicated to characterizing shear layers via 2D hybrid (kinetic ions -- fluid electrons) simulations, we study the dynamical role of nonthermal particles (cosmic rays, CRs), either spontaneously generated or pre-existing. We initialize Kolmogorov-type sinusoidal velocity shear flows unstable to the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, which evolve nonlinearly into turbulence. Particles with large gyroradii act as long-range messengers that promote momentum exchange between layers, hence introducing a form of CR viscosity. Even when not energetically dominant, increasing the CR energy density generally enhances momentum transfer, provided that their gyroradii are smaller than the shear lengthscale. We consider flows ranging from subsonic to supersonic and assess the rate of shear dissipation, the partition of the initial kinetic energy among heating, thermal ion acceleration, CR reacceleration, and magnetic-field amplification, and the maximum energy attained by accelerated particles.

AI.tldr: This study uses 2D hybrid simulations to show that cosmic rays enhance momentum exchange and shear dissipation in turbulent shear layers formed by Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, affecting energy distribution and particle acceleration processes.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of nonthermal particles, specifically cosmic rays, on the dynamical evolution and energy dissipation mechanisms in shear layers subjected to Kelvin--Helmholtz instability.
AI.method: 2D hybrid simulations combining kinetic ions and fluid electrons were used to model sinusoidal velocity shear flows subject to Kelvin--Helmholtz instability evolving into turbulence, with varying CR energy densities and flow regimes (subsonic to supersonic).
AI.result: Increasing CR energy density generally enhances momentum exchange across shear layers via CRs with gyroradii smaller than the shear lengthscale, affecting shear dissipation rates, energy partitioning (heating, ion acceleration, CR reacceleration, magnetic amplification), and leading to efficient particle acceleration.
AI.conclusion: Cosmic rays significantly influence the dynamics of shear layers by enhancing momentum transfer and contributing to shear dissipation processes, even when not energetically dominant, through a mechanism akin to CR viscosity.

title: Constraints on Coupled Dark Energy in the DESI Era
comment: 21 pages, 8 figures. Comments are welcome
summary: We investigate the current viability of a well-known coupled dark energy scenario in which fermionic cold dark matter (DM) interacts with a spin-0 dark energy component through a non-trivial field dependence of the DM mass. This ultra-light scalar mediates a fifth force between DM particles, which can leave signatures on cosmological scales. We use state-of-the-art data on the cosmic microwave background from Planck's CamSpec likelihood, baryon acoustic oscillations from the second DESI data release as well as the supernovae of Type Ia (SNIa) from Pantheon+ and DES-Dovekie. We perform the analysis considering both a flat potential and a Peebles-Ratra (PR) potential for the scalar field in order to assess the impact of the potential slope on the fitting performance of the model. While for a constant potential the scalar field dynamics is insensitive to the sign of the coupling parameter $β$, the PR potential breaks the existing symmetry in the solutions at late times and could induce a difference at the phenomenological level between positive and negative values. We study for the first time if it is actually the case, finding no important asymmetry in the fitting results. In the light of the aforesaid datasets, we find in all cases a peak at $|β|\sim 0.03$ - less pronounced than reported in some recent works -, excluding the no-coupling scenario at $\sim 95\%$ CL. The model is able to explain an effective crossing of the phantom divide, with the equation-of-state parameter lying within the $2σ$ bands of model-agnostic reconstructions. Our results are very robust under changes in the SNIa sample used in the analysis and is not significantly altered when we replace a constant potential with the PR one, although the latter is crucial to produce the aforesaid crossing. In passing, we also provide constraints obtained with the PR potential in the uncoupled case.

AI.tldr: This paper tests a coupled dark energy model with scalar-mediated dark matter interactions using recent cosmological data. It finds evidence favoring a small nonzero coupling (~0.03), explains complex dark energy behavior including phantom divide crossing, shows robustness across datasets and potential choices, and rules out zero coupling at 95% confidence.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to assess the current viability of a coupled dark energy scenario where fermionic cold dark matter interacts with a spin-0 dark energy scalar field affecting the dark matter mass, potentially producing observable cosmological signatures.
AI.method: The study uses recent cosmological data sets including Planck CMB (CamSpec likelihood), baryon acoustic oscillations from DESI, and Type Ia supernovae from Pantheon+ and DES-Dovekie, analyzing both a flat potential and a Peebles-Ratra (PR) potential for the scalar field to evaluate model fitting and the impact of potential slope.
AI.result: The analysis finds a preference for a coupling parameter magnitude around |β|∼0.03, excluding a no-coupling scenario at about 95% confidence level. No significant asymmetry between positive and negative coupling values was found despite the PR potential breaking symmetry in theory. The model explains an effective crossing of the phantom divide (equation-of-state parameter behavior) consistent with observational reconstructions, and results are robust against changes in supernovae samples and potential choice, though the PR potential is essential for the phantom divide crossing.
AI.conclusion: The coupled dark energy model with a coupling parameter around 0.03 remains viable under current cosmological data, and can effectively describe dark energy dynamics including phantom divide crossing, with no strong preference for coupling sign and little effect from potential slope variations. The uncoupled PR potential case was also constrained for comparison.

title: Relativistic Effects on Circumbinary Orbit Stability
comment: Accepted for Publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: With n-body simulations and analytic approximations we study the dynamics and stability of low eccentricity misaligned test particles around binary systems with varying mass fraction and eccentricity. General relativity (GR) plays a primary role in determining the motion of an outer particle since it drives apsidal precession of the binary orbit. The effects of GR can drive particle instability close to the binary orbit, depending upon the binary parameters and the initial inclination of the particle. For the binary parameters we consider, we find instability up to a semimajor axis of about 8 ab, where ab is the binary semimajor axis. In particular, we identify and analyse three different regions of instability that are driven by GR in the phase plane of the initial semimajor axis and the initial inclination of the particle. The results have implications for circumbinary orbits and circumbinary disks on all scales, but are particularly important around supermassive black hole binaries where the effects of GR can be strong.

AI.tldr: This study uses simulations and analytic methods to reveal how general relativity causes instability in misaligned particles orbiting binaries, especially near supermassive black hole binaries, with instability zones extending up to 8 times the binary semimajor axis.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics and stability of low eccentricity misaligned test particles orbiting binary systems with varying mass fraction and eccentricity, especially considering the significant role of general relativity (GR) in shaping particle motion near binaries.
AI.method: Utilized n-body simulations alongside analytic approximations to investigate particle dynamics and stability around binaries, incorporating GR-induced apsidal precession effects within varied binary system parameters and initial particle inclinations.
AI.result: Identified that GR effects can induce particle instability up to approximately 8 times the binary semimajor axis, with three distinct regions of instability mapped in the phase plane of initial semimajor axis and initial inclination. These GR-driven instabilities depend on binary parameters and initial particle inclination.
AI.conclusion: General relativity critically influences the stability of circumbinary orbits, causing significant particle instabilities near binary systems. This insight is crucial for understanding circumbinary disks across scales, notably around supermassive black hole binaries where GR effects are pronounced.

title: Probing Collapsed Dark Matter Halos with Fast Radio Bursts
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables
summary: Observations of ultra-dense substructures in strong lensing systems challenge the standard cosmological model at small scales. Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), as an alternative to the cold and collisionless dark matter (CDM) of the standard cosmological model, provides a natural mechanism for forming such structures via gravothermal core collapse. We show that strong gravitational lensing of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides an effective approach to detecting these substructures and probing dark matter self-interactions. Core-collapsed SIDM halos exhibit steeper central density profiles than CDM halos, enhancing the lensing cross section and producing longer time delays between FRB images. We compute lensing properties of core-collapsed subhalos and host halos, including maximal impact parameters and time-delay distributions. We demonstrate that future all-sky monitors, such as BURSTT, SKA2-Low, and SKA2-Mid, which are expected to detect $10^{5}$--$10^{7}$ FRBs over a decade, can measure time-delay distributions with high statistical significance. Modeling collapsed halos with a cored power-law density profile with inner slope $γ=3$ and assuming no excess beyond the singular isothermal sphere lens model, we show that our strategy can probe self-interaction cross section strengths of $σ_{\text{SI}}/m \gtrsim \min\{18,\, 40λ_{\text{sub}}\}\,\text{cm}^2/\text{g}$, where $λ_{\text{sub}}$ parameterizes the collapse time of a subhalo relative to that of the isolated case.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using strong gravitational lensing of fast radio bursts to detect dense substructures formed by self-interacting dark matter. Core-collapsed SIDM halos create distinct lensing signatures, enabling future FRB surveys to constrain dark matter self-interaction strengths effectively.
AI.motivation: Observations of ultra-dense substructures in strong lensing systems challenge the standard cold dark matter model, motivating alternative dark matter theories such as self-interacting dark matter (SIDM).
AI.method: The paper analyzes gravitational lensing of fast radio bursts (FRBs) by core-collapsed SIDM halos, computing lensing cross sections, maximal impact parameters, and time-delay distributions for FRB images, using a cored power-law density profile to model collapsed halos.
AI.result: The study finds that core-collapsed SIDM halos produce steeper density profiles and longer FRB time delays than CDM halos, enhancing detectability. Future all-sky FRB monitors can measure time-delay distributions with high statistical significance, allowing probing of self-interaction cross sections down to σ_SI/m ≳ min{18, 40λ_sub} cm²/g.
AI.conclusion: Strong lensing of FRBs by core-collapsed SIDM substructures offers a promising probe of dark matter self-interactions, providing constraints on SIDM cross sections that challenge the standard cosmological model at small scales.

title: Mapping the emission and spectral properties of the FRI radio galaxy 3C 449 with LOFAR and the VLA
comment: 26 pages, 37 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The jets and lobes of nearby radio galaxies are ideal laboratories to explore the spectral and dynamical evolution of the radio-emitting plasma that emanates from active galactic nuclei. Here, we present a high-resolution radio continuum study of the low-redshift (z=0.01713), Fanaroff-Riley I (FRI) radio galaxy 3C 449 performed by combining radio data at 145 MHz acquired with the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR) and archival Very Large Array (VLA) data at 1365, 1485, 4985, and 8485 MHz. Our LOFAR maps have angular resolutions of 20"x20" and 6.0"x6.0", and show the full extent of the known radio emission at the highest angular resolution to date. Our spectral index maps show the distribution of the spectrum in the 145-8485 MHz frequency range over a region that extends beyond 2.5'. The average 145-8485 MHz spectrum is consistent with a single power law and stays approximately constant over the inner ~50" of both jets. Beyond ~50", on both source sides, the higher-frequency spectrum steepens, indicating no significant downstream sites of particle acceleration. By modelling the spectrum under the assumption of equipartition and of a constant magnetic field across the source, we derive maps of the highest radiative age of the particles. At the outer edges of both the northern tail and southern lobe, the spectral age is ~150 Myr. If the latter age were representative of the dynamical source age, the average expansion speed of both jets during the source lifetime would be supersonic, with Mach numbers of M~4.1 and M~2.8 for the northern and southern jets, respectively. As numerical simulations of FRI jets suggest that the source's current expansion is subsonic, the high Mach numbers might arise either from the source being highly supersonic for a small fraction of its lifetime or from a severe underestimation of the spectral age due to particle acceleration on scales of hundreds of kpc.

AI.tldr: High-resolution LOFAR and VLA observations of radio galaxy 3C 449 show a mostly constant spectral index in the jets, steepening at outer regions with spectral ages of ~150 Myr, implying potentially supersonic expansion that challenges current models of radio galaxy dynamics.
AI.motivation: To investigate the spectral and dynamical evolution of radio-emitting plasma in jets and lobes of nearby radio galaxies, focusing on the FRI galaxy 3C 449.
AI.method: High-resolution radio continuum observations combining LOFAR data at 145 MHz with archival VLA data at multiple higher frequencies (1365 to 8485 MHz), generating spectral index maps and modeling the spectrum assuming equipartition and constant magnetic field to derive radiative ages.
AI.result: The integrated spectrum follows a single power law over the inner ~50" of the jets, steepening beyond. Spectral ages of ~150 Myr at jet edges suggest potentially supersonic expansion speeds (Mach ~4.1 north, ~2.8 south) if representative of source age, conflicting with simulations indicating subsonic expansion. This suggests either transient supersonic phases or underestimated ages due to ongoing particle acceleration at large scales.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals complex spectral behavior indicative of limited particle acceleration within the jets and raises questions on source expansion dynamics, suggesting revisions to spectral aging estimates or dynamical histories are necessary.

title: Disk instability model incorporating a variable inner disk radius in SS Cyg and U Gem
comment: 11 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in PASJ
summary: Previous theoretical studies indicate that the inner disk in dwarf novae evaporates into a high-temperature, optically thin, and geometrically thick accretion flow during quiescence, with the inner edge moving toward the white dwarf at the onset of an outburst. We incorporate this process into the numerical model developed by Kimura & Osaki (2023) and test the code on two representative dwarf novae, SS Cyg and U Gem. By modeling the inner accretion flow, we calculate the optical, ultraviolet (UV), and X-ray luminosities. Our results show that evaporation suppresses the inside-out outbursts without requiring a radially dependent viscosity parameter in the cold state. The observed time delay between the rise in UV luminosity and the onset of the optical outburst is more than one day, which is successfully reproduced when the inner disk is truncated at several $\times 10^{9}$ cm in the standard evaporation model. However, while the modeled accretion rate at the inner disk edge in U Gem accounts for its quiescent X-ray luminosity, the rate in SS Cyg remains insufficient. This discrepancy in SS Cyg suggests that SS Cyg may require either more efficient evaporation or an additional mass supply into the coronal cavity via gas-stream overflow. By accounting for disk evaporation, our simulations offer a refined version of the disk instability model for dwarf nova outbursts that naturally explains the observed multiwavelength light curves.

AI.tldr: This paper enhances dwarf nova models by including inner disk evaporation, reproducing key multiwavelength observations like UV-optical delays and X-ray luminosities, but notes that certain systems may require extra mechanisms beyond standard evaporation.
AI.motivation: To incorporate disk evaporation processes into numerical models of dwarf novae accretion flows to better understand the multiwavelength observational features during outbursts.
AI.method: Integrated the evaporation of the inner accretion disk into the existing numerical model by Kimura & Osaki (2023) and applied the enhanced model to two dwarf novae, SS Cyg and U Gem. Calculated optical, UV, and X-ray luminosities based on the modeled inner accretion flow.
AI.result: Evaporation suppresses inside-out outbursts without needing a radially dependent viscosity parameter in the cold state. The model successfully reproduces the observed UV-optical delay and X-ray luminosity in U Gem. However, SS Cyg's X-ray luminosity is underpredicted, implying possible additional mechanisms like more efficient evaporation or extra mass supply via gas-stream overflow.
AI.conclusion: Including disk evaporation refines the disk instability model, naturally explaining observed multiwavelength light curves and the UV-optical delay in dwarf novae outbursts, though some discrepancies in specific systems suggest additional physical processes may be involved.

title: Impact of the SNe Ia Magnitude Transition at 20 Mpc on Cosmological Parameter Estimation
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures. Accepted in Phys. Rev. D to appear. The numerical analysis files for the reproduction of the figures are available at a GitHub repository (link in the paper)
summary: We investigate the impact of a late-time transition in the standardized absolute magnitude $M$ on the best-fit values of cosmological parameters using the Pantheon+ dataset. Extending previous analyses which focused on flat $Λ$CDM, we examine this transition within flat $Λ$CDM, wCDM, and CPL cosmologies, as well as a model-independent cosmographic expansion, employing both frequentist ($χ^2$ minimization with \textit{AIC}/\textit{BIC}) and Bayesian (MCMC and Nested Sampling) inference frameworks. We confirm that the data consistently favor a step in absolute magnitude of $ΔM \simeq 0.19~\mathrm{mag}$ at a characteristic distance of $d_{\mathrm{crit}} \approx 20~\mathrm{Mpc}$. The inclusion of this transition leads to a statistically significant improvement in the quality of fit and has a distinct impact on parameter estimation: it induces a systematic increase in the inferred Hubble constant of approximately $2\%$ across all tested models. In contrast, we find that the dynamical parameters governing the background expansion, including the matter density $Ω_m$ and the dark energy equation of state ($w_0, w_a$), remain stable and largely unaffected. These results indicate that the $20~\mathrm{Mpc}$ feature acts primarily as a low-redshift calibration shift rather than a modification of the late-time expansion history.

AI.tldr: A late-time jump in absolute magnitude at 20 Mpc improves model fits and raises the Hubble constant estimate by ~2%, without affecting matter density or dark energy parameters, suggesting a calibration effect rather than a change in cosmological expansion.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether a late-time transition in standardized absolute magnitude M affects cosmological parameter estimation.
AI.method: Use Pantheon+ dataset to analyze flat ΛCDM, wCDM, CPL cosmologies and cosmographic expansion, applying frequentist (χ^2 minimization with AIC/BIC) and Bayesian (MCMC, Nested Sampling) inference methods.
AI.result: Data favor a step change in absolute magnitude ΔM ≈ 0.19 mag at ≈ 20 Mpc, improving fit quality and increasing the inferred Hubble constant by ~2% across models, while matter density Ω_m and dark energy parameters (w_0, w_a) remain stable.
AI.conclusion: The 20 Mpc magnitude transition represents a low-redshift calibration shift affecting Hubble constant estimation rather than altering the late-time expansion dynamics of the universe.

title: Accretion-Mode Transition: The Driver Behind Spectral Changes in Changing-Look AGNs
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, accepted by RAA
summary: The physical origin of optical changing-look AGNs (CLAGNs), characterized by the appearance or disappearance of broad emission lines, is thought to be mainly driven by the variation of the black-hole (BH) accretion rate. In this work, we explore this issue based on a sample of {224} CLAGNs with UV-to-optical continua, where the UV radiation is more sensitive to the accretion state near the BH horizon. We find that the luminosity correlation of $L_{3000}$--$L_{5100}$ at 3000$\rm Å$ and 5100$\rm Å$ becomes steeper at low luminosities (e.g., $L_{3000}\lesssim10^{44}\rm erg/s$), where the sources with high luminosities are roughly consistent with the prediction of a standard accretion disk. At lower luminosities, the observations are more consistent with the prediction of a truncated disk. The whole sample has a median bolometric Eddington ratio of $\sim$2.2\%, which is consistent with the critical value for state transition in X-ray binaries. Such transitions can significantly alter the UV-to-optical continuum, largely due to variations in the truncation radius, even when the change in the overall accretion rate is minimal. The deficit of ionization photons resulting from an increase in the truncation radius will lead to the weakening or disappearance of broad lines, which triggers the AGN changing-look.

AI.tldr: This study on 224 CLAGNs shows that optical changing-look behavior arises from accretion state transitions causing disk truncation, reducing ionizing photons and broad emission lines, with minimal changes in accretion rate.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origin of optical changing-look AGNs (CLAGNs), especially the cause of their characteristic appearance or disappearance of broad emission lines, by exploring the connection to black-hole accretion rate variations.
AI.method: Analyzing a sample of 224 CLAGNs with UV-to-optical continuum data, focusing on the luminosity correlation between 3000 Å and 5100 Å emission, and comparing observations with theoretical predictions of accretion disk models (standard vs truncated) and Eddington ratios relevant for state transitions.
AI.result: Found that at high luminosities, CLAGNs follow standard accretion disk predictions, whereas at low luminosities (below ~10^{44} erg/s), observations favor truncated disk models. The median bolometric Eddington ratio (~2.2%) aligns with state transition values from X-ray binaries, explaining continuum changes driven by truncation radius variations with minimal accretion rate change. This leads to fewer ionizing photons, weakening or eliminating broad emission lines and causing the changing-look phenomena.
AI.conclusion: The changing-look behavior in optical AGNs is primarily driven by accretion state transitions that cause changes in the disk truncation radius, altering UV-to-optical continuum and ionizing photon output, rather than large variations in overall accretion rate.

title: Illuminating the Local Universe: Large-Scale Structure from ZTF Type Ia Supernovae
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, submitted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Within the volume-limited subsample at $z<0.06$ of the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) DR2 sample, we confirm a statistically significant excess of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) at $z \simeq 0.02$-$0.04$, previously reported but not explained by survey selection effects. Forward simulations assuming a uniform volumetric SN Ia rate and realistic ZTF detection efficiencies fail to reproduce the feature at the $5$-$7σ$ level. We also detect an excess in the rates compared to our survey simulations at $z \simeq 0.08$ and $0.14$, albeit at smaller significance. To investigate the origin of these inhomogeneities, we compare the observed SN distribution to constrained reconstructions of the local matter density field from the Manticore project, based on Bayesian forward modelling of the 2M++ galaxy catalogue. While SN overdensities are spatially associated with prominent nearby structures such as the Perseus, Coma, and Hercules superclusters, the amplitude of the SN excesses significantly exceeds that expected from matter overdensities alone. By reconstructing a redshift-dependent volumetric SN Ia rate, we find that local enhancements can reach factors of two to five within specific clusters, while the sample-averaged rate remains consistent with previous low-redshift measurements. These results indicate that the SN Ia rate is not a linear tracer of the underlying matter density and suggest a strong environmental dependence in dense structures. We discuss possible physical origins and highlight the implications for low-redshift SN cosmology, including correlated peculiar velocities and additional covariance beyond standard linear corrections.

AI.tldr: This paper finds significant excesses of Type Ia supernovae at low redshift correlated with large-scale structures, suggesting environmental effects on SN rates that challenge simple linear models and impact cosmological analyses at low redshift.
AI.motivation: The study aims to investigate the unexpected excess of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) at specific low redshifts observed in the ZTF DR2 sample, which was not explained by survey selection effects.
AI.method: The researchers used forward simulations with a uniform volumetric SN Ia rate and ZTF detection efficiencies, compared observed SN distributions to local matter density reconstructions from the Manticore project based on Bayesian modeling of the 2M++ galaxy catalogue, and reconstructed a redshift-dependent volumetric SN Ia rate.
AI.result: They confirmed a statistically significant excess of SNe Ia around z~0.02-0.04 and smaller excesses at z~0.08 and 0.14. The excesses associate spatially with large-scale structures but exceed expectations from matter overdensities alone. Local SN rates can be enhanced by a factor of 2 to 5 in clusters, implying a strong environmental dependence. The overall average rate remains consistent with previous measurements.
AI.conclusion: The SN Ia rate does not linearly trace matter density and shows strong dependence on environment in dense structures. This affects interpretations in low-redshift SN cosmology, including peculiar velocity correlations and covariance beyond standard corrections.

title: Revisiting the angular size-redshift cosmological test with milliarcsecond radio structures in active galactic nuclei
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A; 10 pages, 6 figures
summary:
VLBI measurements of the sizes of compact extragalactic radio sources, jetted active galactic nuclei, provide data for probing the angular size--redshift relation, offering a complementary test to other distance--redshift methods.
  We analyse a significantly expanded dataset to reassess the angular size--redshift relation and its potential for constraining cosmological model parameters, focusing on the matter density parameter $Ω_{\mathrm{m}}$ in a flat $Λ$ Cold Dark Matter Universe. This is the first major update of the compact-source angular size test in the past quarter of a century, using a dataset an order of magnitude larger than in previous studies.
  MCMC analysis on real data and on multiple mock catalogues to evaluate parameter constraints in the presence of observational scatter. In addition, we conducted a test with 100 randomized catalogues created by shuffling redshifts while preserving other observables. We also explored how astrophysical parameters depend on fixed cosmological models with different $Ω_{\mathrm{m}}$ values.
  The randomization test showed that the posterior distributions from randomized data do not overlap with those from real observations, confirming that the measured angular size--redshift relation is physically meaningful. The astrophysical model parameter that describes the redshift dependence of the source angular size exhibits degeneracy with $Ω_{\mathrm{m}}$. Simulated mock catalogues indicate that the method is able to constrain $Ω_{\mathrm{m}}$ if the data scatter is below $\sim20\%$. Scaling estimates suggest that high-quality data of samples of several thousands to $\sim 100\,000$ sources, a standardisation calibration approach, and/or refining sample selection criteria are needed to fully exploit the potential of the angular size--redshift test with this type of objects (abridged).

AI.tldr: Using a significantly larger VLBI dataset, this study updates the angular size--redshift relation test, confirming its validity and potential to constrain cosmological parameters like Ω_m, while highlighting the need for improved data quality and calibration to fully leverage this method.
AI.motivation: To reassess the angular size--redshift relation using VLBI measurements of compact extragalactic radio sources with an expanded dataset to constrain the matter density parameter Ω_m in a flat ΛCDM Universe, improving on past studies by leveraging a larger data sample.
AI.method: Analysis of an order of magnitude larger VLBI dataset using MCMC techniques on real and mock catalogues, including randomized redshift tests and exploration of astrophysical parameter dependencies under varying Ω_m values.
AI.result: The angular size--redshift relation is confirmed as physically meaningful; degeneracy exists between astrophysical parameters and Ω_m; the method can constrain Ω_m if observational scatter is below ~20%; high-quality, large-sample data and improved calibration or selection are required to maximize potential.
AI.conclusion: The VLBI-based angular size--redshift relation is a viable complementary cosmological probe, but achieving precise constraints on cosmological parameters demands better data quality and quantity alongside refined calibration methods.

title: Acoustic instability at shock-wave precursors
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Magnetic field amplification is an integral part of the process of particle acceleration at non-relativistic shocks. It is necessary to reach the maximum energies required by observations, especially in supernova remnants, thought to be sources of the bulk of Galactic cosmic rays. Such amplification can be caused by the acoustic instability that develops when small density perturbations interact with the cosmic-ray pressure gradient in the upstream of a cosmic-ray-modified shock. The vorticity induced by the nonlinear development of the instability may lead to turbulence, which amplifies the pre-existing magnetic fields. To study this phenomenon, we use the PLUTO code to carry out 2D (and some 3D) magnetohydrodynamical simulations of the evolution of small density perturbations in the presence of an assigned cosmic-ray pressure gradient. Adopting more realistic values of Mach number and cosmic-ray acceleration efficiency than previously assumed in the literature, we show that the acoustic instability can transform small density perturbations into large nonlinear structures while the fluid crosses the precursor region of a cosmic-ray-modified shock. We study the power spectrum of turbulent magnetic fluctuations that may be important to scatter particles. We comment on the possible constructive interference between acoustic and non-resonant streaming instabilities. We discuss limitations of previous and current numerical investigations in accessing spatial scales where turbulence is expected to turn nonlinear, and outline perspectives for future investigations.

AI.tldr: This paper uses advanced MHD simulations to demonstrate that acoustic instability can amplify magnetic fields in cosmic-ray-modified shocks through turbulence generated by nonlinear density perturbations, aiding particle acceleration in supernova remnants, while highlighting challenges in simulating nonlinear turbulence fully.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of magnetic field amplification via acoustic instability in particle acceleration at non-relativistic shocks, particularly in supernova remnants as sources of Galactic cosmic rays.
AI.method: Perform 2D and some 3D magnetohydrodynamical simulations using the PLUTO code, modeling evolution of small density perturbations under an assigned cosmic-ray pressure gradient with realistic Mach numbers and cosmic-ray acceleration efficiencies.
AI.result: The acoustic instability can amplify small density perturbations into large nonlinear structures in the shock precursor, generating turbulence that enhances magnetic field fluctuations important for particle scattering. The study also notes potential interaction with other instabilities and identifies limitations in resolving nonlinear turbulence scales.
AI.conclusion: Acoustic instability driven turbulence is a viable mechanism for magnetic field amplification in cosmic-ray-modified shocks, facilitating efficient particle acceleration; however, current numerical methods face challenges in fully capturing nonlinear turbulent scales, necessitating further study.

title: Do equation of state parametrizations of dark energy faithfully capture the dynamics of the late universe?
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables
summary: We investigate how strongly late-time inferences about DE dynamics depend on the functional prior used to represent the expansion history. Using identical late-time combinations of CC, DESI BAO measurements, the Pantheon+ SN1a sample, and the H0DN prior, we compare a node-based reconstruction of the reduced Hubble function $E(z)$ with a representative family of smooth low-dimensional DE EoS parametrizations, including CPL. Over the redshift range constrained by the data, both approaches yield consistent $H(z)$, and, in the absence of H0DN, compatible values of $H_0$. However, a clear method dependence emerges at intermediate redshift ($z\sim1.7$): the reconstruction favors stronger deceleration, $q_{\rm Rec}(1.7)\simeq0.56-0.61$, whereas the smooth parametrizations cluster at $q(1.7)\simeq0.32-0.40$, implying a persistent $\sim2-3σ$ discrepancy across dataset combinations and parametrizations. For the EoS-based parametrizations, whose effective DE densities remain positive by construction, the preferred $w_{\rm DE}(1.7)<-1$ values correspond to NECB-violating (phantom-like) behaviour, but this is a less robust discriminator as $w_{\rm DE}$ becomes ill-conditioned as $ρ_{\rm DE}\to0$. In the effective-fluid mapping, the reconstruction accommodates the same late-time kinematical preference through a rapid descent of $ρ_{\rm DE}(z)$ toward very small values and a sign change, whereas the EoS-based parametrizations absorb it through smoother, and in several cases NECB-violating, evolution over $z\sim1-2$. Although the reconstruction improves the best-fit likelihood, especially with H0DN, Bayesian evidence continues to favor the simpler parametric descriptions. Our results isolate $z\sim1.5-2$ as the key window in which EoS-based DE parametrizations can compress localized kinematic structure and associated features of DE that are still permitted by current late-time data.

AI.tldr: This study compares node-based and parametric methods for reconstructing dark energy dynamics from late-time data, revealing method-dependent discrepancies at intermediate redshift, with implications for the choice of functional priors in cosmological inference.
AI.motivation: To examine how late-time dark energy (DE) dynamics inferences depend on the choice of functional prior representing the cosmic expansion history.
AI.method: Comparison of a node-based reconstruction of the reduced Hubble function E(z) with smooth low-dimensional DE equation of state (EoS) parametrizations, including CPL, using late-time cosmological data sets such as CC, DESI BAO, Pantheon+ SN1a, and H0DN prior.
AI.result: Both approaches yield consistent H(z) measures and compatible H0 values without H0DN, but differ prominently at intermediate redshift (z~1.7) where reconstruction shows stronger deceleration than smooth parametrizations, leading to a 2-3σ discrepancy. The reconstruction allows for rapid changes and sign flips in DE density, while EoS parametrizations imply smoother, sometimes NECB-violating phantom-like behaviors. Reconstruction improves fit likelihoods, yet Bayesian evidence favors simpler parametric models.
AI.conclusion: Late-time DE inferences strongly depend on the assumed functional prior, particularly at z~1.5-2, a crucial window where EoS parametrizations compress localized kinematic structures and DE features allowed by current data, highlighting the impact of prior choice on interpreting DE dynamics.

title: POLARIS: A Sparse Radial Neutrino Telescope Design for the Pacific Ocean
comment: Submitted to ApJL
summary: The cubic-kilometer neutrino telescopes have opened neutrino astronomy as an observational discipline. The recent detection of KM3-230213A, the highest-energy neutrino ever observed at ~220 PeV, as a near-horizontal muon track underscores that the ultra-high-energy frontier is accessed through horizontal directions where the Earth's opacity above ~100 TeV confines the observable sky to a narrow band around and above the horizon. Yet extending general-purpose detector architectures into this regime requires disproportionate increases in instrumentation, cost, and logistical complexity. A compelling alternative is to deploy specialized detectors that target this natural geometry. POLARIS (Pacific Ocean Large Area Radial Instrumented Sparse array) is a sparse planar deep-water Cherenkov array optimized for neutrino-induced muon tracks from horizontal directions in the multi-TeV to PeV regime. By rotating the conventional vertical string layout into a radial planar configuration, the detector presents maximal cross-section to horizontal tracks while naturally suppressing the down-going atmospheric background. With only 1100 optical modules, the five-arm design reaches point source and diffuse flux sensitivities at PeV energies competitive with detectors deploying several times more instrumentation. As a dedicated $ν_μ$ track detector, POLARIS provides the muon-flavor channel that tau-optimized experiments such as TAMBO and Trinity do not cover, enabling full flavor composition measurements from astrophysical sources. Using the Prometheus simulation framework, this study demonstrates that targeted sparse geometries can open new discovery space at the high-energy frontier at a fraction of the cost of general-purpose arrays.

AI.tldr: POLARIS is a novel, cost-effective, planar Cherenkov neutrino detector optimized for horizontal muon tracks at PeV energies, delivering competitive sensitivity with fewer modules and enabling full flavor neutrino composition measurements, thus opening new discovery space in ultra-high-energy neutrino astronomy.
AI.motivation: Extending general-purpose neutrino detectors to the ultra-high-energy horizontal regime is challenging due to increased instrumentation, cost, and complexity.
AI.method: Designing and simulating POLARIS, a sparse planar deep-water Cherenkov array with a radial layout optimized for detecting horizontal neutrino-induced muon tracks in the multi-TeV to PeV energy range; using the Prometheus simulation framework to evaluate performance.
AI.result: POLARIS achieves point source and diffuse neutrino flux sensitivities at PeV energies comparable to much larger detectors with fewer optical modules, effectively suppressing atmospheric backgrounds and enabling full flavor composition measurements.
AI.conclusion: Specialized, optimized detector geometries like POLARIS can efficiently access the ultra-high-energy horizontal neutrino frontier, providing competitive sensitivity at reduced cost and complementing other tau-optimized experiments to enhance astrophysical neutrino studies.

title: Probing Scalar-Tensor-Induced Gravitational Waves in the nHz Band: $\texttt{NANOGrav}$ and SKA
comment: 30 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables
summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the $\texttt{NANOGrav 15-year}$ dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. Our results show that the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive detections of the SGWB.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational waves induced by scalar-tensor mixing during early cosmological matter-dominated phases, showing they can explain recent pulsar timing data and be detected by future observatories.
AI.motivation: Investigate scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves as a cosmological source for the stochastic gravitational wave background and their potential to explain recent pulsar timing array data.
AI.method: Computed STGWs generated during generic matter-dominated eras and early matter-dominated epochs with transitions to radiation domination, using Poisson gauge and including linear-order contributions.
AI.result: Found that STGW energy density dilutes rapidly in pure matter domination but remains significant during brief early matter domination; STGWs could explain NANOGrav 15-year data and be detected by future instruments like the SKA.
AI.conclusion: Scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves from early matter-dominated phases are promising candidates for the stochastic gravitational wave background and potential targets for upcoming gravitational wave observations.

title: Gravitational Gertsenshtein-Zeldovich mechanism for the Association between GW190425 and FRB 20190425A
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure
summary: The temporal and spatial coincidence between the gravitational wave (GW) event GW190425 and the fast radio burst (FRB) event FRB 20190425A raises the intriguing possibility of a physical connection between the two. The widely discussed possibility invoking the collapse of a supermassive neutron star as the merger product suffers the inconsistency between the model prediction and the measured inclination angle of the system. Here, we propose a novel physical mechanism to account for the association. We envisage a magnetar located at about 2.5 light hours away from the binary neutron star merger site. The kiloherz GWs generated by the merger are converted into kiloherz electromagnetic (EM) radiation via the Gertsenshtein-Zeldovich (GZ) effect near the magnetar. Subsequent inverse Compton scattering off the kilohertz EM waves by relativistic particles generates the observed gigahertz FRB emission. Our calculation reveals that, with appropriate parameter choices, the properties of FRB 20190425A can be reproduced.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that gravitational waves from a neutron star merger convert to electromagnetic waves near a nearby magnetar, producing the fast radio burst FRB 20190425A, successfully explaining the observed coincidence with event GW190425.
AI.motivation: To explore a plausible physical connection between the gravitational wave event GW190425 and the fast radio burst event FRB 20190425A, overcoming inconsistencies in existing models.
AI.method: Propose a novel mechanism involving a magnetar about 2.5 light hours away from the neutron star merger, where kiloherz gravitational waves are converted into electromagnetic waves via the Gertsenshtein-Zeldovich effect, followed by inverse Compton scattering producing the observed fast radio burst.
AI.result: Calculations demonstrate that with suitable parameters, the proposed mechanism can reproduce the observed properties of FRB 20190425A.
AI.conclusion: The newly proposed mechanism provides a consistent explanation for the temporal and spatial coincidence of GW190425 and FRB 20190425A, addressing limitations of previous models.

title: The spectrum of the persistent radio source associated with FRB 20190417A
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A Letters. 4 pages main text + 2 pages appendices
summary: Persistent radio sources (PRSs) are (sub-)parsec-scale compact non-thermal continuum sources associated with some repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs). Their nature is debated, but their properties provide insights into the FRB environment and progenitors. We measure the spectrum of the recently confirmed PRS associated with FRB 20190417A. Spectral features such as the self-absorption and cooling break can be used to constrain the age and size of PRSs and test theoretical models. We present observations made with the 1.26 GHz upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) and observations from the 6 GHz Karl Jansky Very Large Array (VLA). With complementary archival data and the LOw Frequency ARray Two Meter Sky Survey (LoTSS), we characterise the spectrum of the PRS between 144 MHz and 6 GHz. The spectrum follows a power-law behaviour at gigahertz frequencies. The source is not detected at 144 MHz down to a $2σ=170 \; {\rm μJy}$ sensitivity. We modelled the spectrum with a broken power law, obtaining a spectral index $α= 0.20 \pm 0.05$ between 1-6 GHz. We placed a lower limit on the turn-over frequency of $> 370$ MHz ($95\%$ confidence). The flat spectrum and low-frequency turn-over of the target are consistent with the spectral properties predicted for magneto-ionic nebulae, inflated behind the supernova ejecta by a flaring young magnetar. Considering the multi-zone magnetar wind nebula scenario, we estimate an age of $t< 250$ yr and a radius of $R< 0.4$ pc for the target, which would thus be slightly older than the PRSs associated with FRB 20121102A and FRB 20190520B.

AI.tldr: This study characterizes the spectrum of the PRS linked to FRB 20190417A across 144 MHz to 6 GHz, finding a flat power-law spectrum with a low-frequency turnover, consistent with a magnetar wind nebula scenario; it estimates the PRS to be younger than 250 years and under 0.4 pc in size.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature of persistent radio sources (PRSs) associated with repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) and gain insights into the FRB environment and progenitors.
AI.method: Measured the spectrum of the PRS associated with FRB 20190417A using observations from the uGMRT at 1.26 GHz, the Karl Jansky VLA at 6 GHz, complemented by archival data and the LoTSS at 144 MHz to characterize the spectrum between 144 MHz and 6 GHz; modeled the spectrum with a broken power law to determine spectral indices and turn-over frequency.
AI.result: The PRS spectrum follows a power-law at gigahertz frequencies with a spectral index α=0.20 ± 0.05 between 1-6 GHz; no detection at 144 MHz down to 2σ=170 μJy; a lower limit on the turn-over frequency >370 MHz (95% confidence) was obtained; the flat spectrum and low-frequency turn-over are consistent with magneto-ionic nebulae from a flaring young magnetar; estimated target age <250 years and radius <0.4 pc, slightly older than similar PRSs.
AI.conclusion: The spectral properties and constraints on age and size support the model of the PRS being a magneto-ionic nebula inflated by a young magnetar wind behind supernova ejecta, providing evidence for the link between young magnetars and FRBs.

title: The role of accretion efficiency, natal kicks, and angular momentum transport in the formation of the Gaia black holes
comment: 20 pages, comments welcome
summary: Gaia has the potential to deliver several tens of new dormant black holes (BHs) with low-mass stellar companions (hereafter, Gaia BHs) in the upcoming fourth data release. Three Gaia BHs are already known, but their formation pathways remain uncertain. Here, we perform a large parametric study to explore the formation of Gaia BHs from isolated binary systems with the population-synthesis code SEVN and compare our models with the properties of the three already reported Gaia BHs. Specifically, we explore the impact of accretion efficiency, mass transfer stability, natal kicks, angular momentum transport, and core-collapse supernova prescriptions.
